title: Butternut Squash Ravioli with Brown Butter and Sage
changes_from_base: Ricotta filling replaced by roasted butternut squash with Parmesan and nutmeg; sauce is brown butter with crisp sage and a little lemon instead of plain butter.
summary: This follows the same dough, filling and sealing method as our classic ricotta ravioli, with a roasted butternut squash filling in place of ricotta and a nutty brown butter and sage sauce instead of plain melted butter.
equipment: roasting tray lined with baking paper
pastry brush and small bowl of water
6-7 cm round cutter or fluted pasta wheel

ingredients.item: "00" or plain flour, plus extra for dusting
fine sea salt or table salt
fine semolina, for dusting the tray
butternut squash, about 1000 g, halved lengthways and seeded
fine sea salt or table salt
fine salt for 4 litres of pasta water (0.8%)
ingredients.note: about 5.25 tsp; most of it goes down the drain

steps.title: Roast the squash
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) at least 20 minutes ahead, rub the cut sides of the squash with olive oil and roast cut side down for 45-55 minutes, until completely soft and caramelised at the edges.

steps.title: Mash and season the filling
steps.text: Once the squash is cool enough to handle, after about 10 minutes, scoop out the flesh (around 400g) and mash or blitz it smooth with the Parmesan, nutmeg, salt and pepper. If the mixture looks wet, stir it in a hot dry pan for 3-5 minutes to steam off extra moisture, since a dry filling seals more reliably inside the pasta. Chill the filling before using.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Tip the flour onto the worktop and shape a mound with a 12cm well, then add the eggs, yolks and salt. Beat with a fork, drawing in flour from the inner wall until a soft paste forms, then fold in the rest with a bench scraper.

steps.title: Knead until smooth
steps.text: Knead for 8-10 minutes, pushing with the heel of your hand and folding the dough back on itself, until it's smooth, firm and springs back slowly when poked. The egg, at around 67% of the flour's weight, gives the dough its firm, silky texture once the gluten has developed. Wet your hands if it cracks, or dust in a little extra flour if it feels tacky.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.text: Wrap the dough and leave it to rest for 30-60 minutes at room temperature, giving the gluten time to relax so it rolls out without springing back.

steps.title: Roll, fill and cut
steps.text: Roll, fill and cut the ravioli exactly as for the classic ricotta version: thin sheets down to under 1mm, 2 tsp mounds of filling 5cm apart, water-sealed edges with the air pressed out, then cut and laid on semolina-dusted trays.

steps.title: Brown the butter
steps.text: Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat and swirl the pan for 3-4 minutes, until the foam subsides, the milk solids turn a hazelnut brown and the butter smells distinctly nutty. Add the sage leaves and fry for 30 seconds until they turn crisp, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the lemon juice, which stops the butter browning any further.

steps.title: Cook and glaze
steps.text: Bring 4 litres of water to the boil with the 32g of salt and cook the ravioli in 2 batches for 3-4 minutes. Lift them straight into the brown butter with a slotted spoon along with 80ml of the cooking water, then swirl over medium heat for 1 minute to glaze. Serve with the Parmesan for the table.

tips: Roast the squash until it's truly soft and caramelised at the edges — underdone squash makes a watery, bland filling.
Steam off any extra moisture from the mashed squash before filling the ravioli, or the parcels will be prone to splitting.
Watch the butter closely once it starts foaming — it goes from nutty brown to burnt in under a minute.
Add the lemon juice off the heat straight after the sage crisps, since it's what halts the browning at the right point.
storage: Uncooked ravioli keep in the fridge for up to 1 day on a floured tray, or freeze in a single layer for up to 1 month and cook from frozen with an extra minute. Reheat cooked leftovers gently in a pan until piping hot. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
